reasoning:
Attempt A wins. Its Luau code is about as good as B's, and it is the only one that passes every check.

The deciding difference is the StarterKit model file. A writes the five counts as plain JSON numbers, and the build check confirms they become number attributes, as the task asks. B writes each count in the explicit `{ "Float64": n }` form. The built-place check reports B's attributes as differing from the expected numbers, and that failure traces to B's own file. I couldn't confirm what Rojo 7.7.1 does with the explicit form, so I took off points for that criterion but didn't fail B outright.

Apart from that, both attempts handle players who joined early, give 0 with a warning for a missing attribute, wait until all counts exist, and retry SetCore inside pcall. A also keeps the feature in its own script files.

criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json with className Configuration, mounted at ReplicatedStorage.Shared.
Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0, Wood 10 are plain JSON numbers, and the build check confirms they become number attributes.
StarterKit.server.luau is under ServerScriptService and StarterKit.client.luau is under StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: 4. Reads StarterKit at the real path and covers every type
criteria.note: Finds the kit with ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("StarterKit", true) and asserts it is a Configuration, loops over BlockTypes.List, and gives 0 with a warning when an attribute is missing (it also floors and clamps the value).

criteria.criterion: 5. Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: Loops over Players:GetPlayers() with task.spawn, waits on AttributeChanged until every count is a number, then calls SetCore inside pcall with up to 20 retries 0.5 s apart.
Only new files were added, and luau-lsp, selene, StyLua, and rojo build all pass.

strengths: Every check passes, including the number-attribute build check
Validates attributes defensively and warns when one is missing
The SetCore retry loop is solid and the notification is sent once
Covers players who joined before the server script connected
weaknesses: The recursive FindFirstChild could pick up a different object named StarterKit, though the assert limits the risk
The client's top-level wait yields the script; harmless here
